svg.title: RIEMANN · MAP R1 — Main.lean, theorem by theorem: the five theorems, the statements they are made of, and the chain of reductions that proves them
svg.desc: The formal proof is 164,464 Lean files with no comments; the blueprint reads it as 416 statements and the edges between them. This diagram draws the five theorems of Main.lean, the definitions they are stated with, and the chain of reductions by which the hard one, GRH, half-plane form, reaches the theorems that the chapters prove. Each node is one blueprint statement: the Lean declaration it stands for, as the blueprint's facts file records its signature, the statement in words, how its proof goes, and what it uses and is used by. Read it from the foot up: the five theorems are at the bottom, and everything above is what their proofs use. No Lean was built for the blueprint or for this diagram: the edges were resolved from the source text and some are wrong, and whether the formal proof is correct is a question for the kernel checks of band 5. Map mode: nothing of the blueprint's text or the proof's source is quoted; each card gives the statement's title, kind, provenance, Lean name and location, and its edges.

text.tspan: the claims, as the mirror states them

svg.text: The claims. Main.lean states the five theorems the Comparator config names, each as a Prop that Statements.lean defines from Mathlib's riemannZeta and DirichletCharacter.LFunction;
The proof terms rhOfAll, allChi, claimAll and critAll are where the five theorems enter the 164,464 files of the proof. Everything above them in this diagram is what those terms unfold to.
The permitted axioms are propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice: a proof using any other is rejected before a kernel runs.
src/Main.lean (every theorem) and src/Statements.lean (every definition) at 2dea990069 · the axioms from comparator.json

text.tspan: The five stages of the proof (the architecture chapter's own list)

svg.text: Galois … Not quoted in map mode: the blueprint's text and the proof's source stay their authors'. The blueprint link below has both.
The five stages are: Galois representations, the Tate–Shafarevich bound, families, slope data and the core inequality, Landau's theorem; one chapter each, as diagram R2 draws them.

Read right to left: each theorem reduces the half-plane claim to the one on its left, and GRH from Galois representations gathers the whole chain. An arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A.

text.tspan: 5 · Reference: the five theorems, the depth of the proof, and what has been checked
The theorems of Main.lean, and the blueprint node that carries each
Statements by depth from the main theorems (the diagram's own count)

svg.text: A statement's depth is the fewest uses edges from one of the three theorems nothing else uses (The Riemann
Hypothesis and the two critical-line forms) down to it. The five theorems of Main.lean sit at depths 0 and 1.
7 of the blueprint's 416 statements are reached by no edge from the main theorems: the blueprint's remarks
and a few results whose users it did not resolve.
Published results sit mostly at depths 4 and 5: the new argument is the top of the tree and rests on the

text.tspan: Checked and proved: what is known about the formal proof

svg.text: lake build Main compiles every file of the submission; a successful build is a check by the kernel of Lean v4.33.1, the version the project pins.
The mirror's notes list independent complete builds, and compare their compiled files with the checksums the author published: in the complete
lake comparator exports the five theorems and replays them in kernels independent of Lean's own, Lean paranoid and nanoda, allowing only
the three axioms of comparator.json. The notes say its output will be added when the run finishes. At the state drawn, no result is recorded.
No Lean was built for the blueprint. Its uses edges were resolved from identifiers in the source text, and its README says some are wrong and
that every proof status reads *absent*. This diagram inherits both limits. A node here says what a statement is, not that it is proved.

Sources: riemann-blueprint at 137d976026 (the front matter, statement and proof of every drawn node; lean-facts.json for every signature, file and line; the architecture chapter's introduction); leanprover-community/riemann-hypothesis at 2dea990069 (src/Main.lean, src/Statements.lean, comparator.json, verification/NOTES.md). The depth table and the abridgements are the diagram's own, computed or cut as marked.
